crossRefs.note: “Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
having a good conscience. Thus, while you are spoken against as evildoers, they may be disappointed who curse your good…
For it is better, if it is God’s will, that you suffer for doing well than for doing evil.
The law came in that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly;
What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under law, but under grace? May it never be!
What shall we say then? Is the law sin? May it never be! However, I wouldn’t have known sin, except through the law.…
For there are certain men who crept in secretly, even those who were long ago written about for this condemnation…

translations.web: Why not (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say), “Let’s do evil, that good may come?” Those who say so are justly condemned.
translations.bsb: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!
translations.kjv: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.
translations.asv: and why not (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say), Let us do evil, that good may come? whose condemnation is just.
